The report also applies participation-rate criteria (85% of selected schools and 85% of selected students within participating schools, with a weighted overall participation rate of 75%), using replacement schools when needed; countries not meeting requirements even after replacement are reported separately. data.outcome_summary: ICCS 2009 European Report summarizes findings from the ICCS 2009 European module administered to Grade 8 students (or Grade 9 when Grade 8 average age was below 13.5) in 24 European countries, using a two-stage cluster sample (PPS school sampling, then intact class sampling). Students completed an international cognitive test (80 items in rotated booklets), an international student questionnaire, and a European cognitive test and European questionnaire; the European cognitive test was not scaled into a common EU knowledge scale due to unsatisfactory scaling properties, so EU-related item results are reported separately. The report also uses teacher, school principal, and national contexts survey data to contextualize civic and citizenship education. Outcomes include both cognitive knowledge (e.g., percentages correct on EU laws/policies and euro items) and affective/behavioral questionnaire scales (standardized to mean 50, SD 10 for equally weighted national samples meeting participation requirements). The report emphasizes cross-country variation and associations between constructs (e.g., self-reported EU knowledge and civic knowledge; European identity and attitudes), while noting that the excerpt does not document PV or missing-data handling procedures for any analytic model.
